old: When I changes at constant L, the kinetic energy $\frac{L^2}{2I}$ changes; energy is not conserved in such cases
new: When I changes at constant L, the rotational kinetic energy $\frac{L^2}{2I}$ changes; it increases when I decreases, because internal forces do work, and decreases when I increases. Kinetic energy is not conserved, but total energy still is
fixes: Clarified that only KE (not total energy) is not conserved when I changes at constant L
